measured-scalar.description: The latest scalar emitted by a repeatable measurement source. Authored lf-num text freezes the value a version states; the source snapshot records whether that measurement ran again.

text-document.description: UTF-8 text from a file or a selected line range.

lf-ask.description: A complete question for the user, with its context and one answer widget.
lf-ask.x-instructions: Begin with a direct heading that states the question without relying on surrounding prose. Include the evidence needed to answer and exactly one non-quoted widget declaring a local Ask through x-awaits. Keep an ordinary semantic section around the Ask when the document needs a section landmark.
lf-ask.x-example:
What should a full store do?

The beta never reached the cap. This decides what the first workspace at it sees.

Drop the oldest documents Editing continues. My take: this keeps work moving without losing server data. Pause offline editing Nothing leaves.

lf-gloss.description: A short explanation the reader can open beside a phrase without leaving its sentence.
lf-gloss.x-instructions: Write a self-contained explanation at the first useful occurrence rather than on every repetition. Keep the phrase out of authored parentheses: print adds the explanation as a parenthetical note.
lf-gloss.x-example: Deploy through a <lf-gloss tip="A thin, end-to-end path through the real system.">walking skeleton</lf-gloss> before parallelizing.

lf-num.description: A measured scalar embedded in prose, tied to the snapshot that established it.
lf-num.x-instructions: Write the displayed value with its unit as the element text. Bind source to the repeatable measurement feed and set at to the updated instant leaf data set printed for that snapshot. Read authoring-evidence.md, Measured facts, for measurement and staleness checks. Use via when the source id alone leaves the command or query unclear.
lf-num.x-example: The import now takes <lf-num source="import-latency" at="2026-08-27T09:00:00Z" via="uv run bench-import">184 ms</lf-num> at p95.

lf-text-document.description: A file-backed text document supplied through Leaf data, with optional syntax coloring.
lf-text-document.x-instructions: Bind source to the page-owned feed. Use label when its source id would not name the document clearly. Put it inside ordinary details or an lf-tab when the document should begin collapsed or in a separate view.

lf-annotation-rail.description: An authored-flow rail for Threads, Asks, action and status contributions, updates, and the active comment editor.
lf-annotation-rail.x-instructions: Select data-annotations=page on body and place one empty rail with a stable id where the document should show annotations. Allocate its width and height in page CSS; it scrolls within that box. Omit it to use the core Threads panel. Native disclosures retain their open state and the shared Thread renderer owns conversations and replies.

lf-toc.description: An outline of the document’s h2–h6 headings for navigating its sections and showing the reader’s position.
lf-toc.x-instructions: Set max-level when deeper headings are local detail rather than navigation destinations; omit it to include h2–h6. Use stable authored section, title-group, or heading ids for links that must keep their target across versions; generated heading ids are not addresses for comments or page state. Write the element empty with a stable id.
lf-toc.x-example:
Migration plan

Prepare

Take a snapshot.

Check capacity

Leave headroom for the copy.

Move

Shift one cohort at a time.

lf-activity.description: A newest-first feed of the page’s comments, actions, reports, and published revisions.
lf-activity.x-instructions: Put the feed last in the column or in a pane of its own. Write it empty with a stable id.

lf-options.description: Alternatives the user can choose individually or as a set to answer a question.
lf-options.x-instructions: Keep shared premises and evidence with the group; lf-ask can frame its question and context. Keep each alternative's case and decision-relevant evidence inside its lf-option. Use multiple wherever two selections can both hold; leave it off for mutually exclusive alternatives. The built-in Another option field accepts unlisted answers, so author the alternatives you mean without a catch-all option. Use for only to select sections or work items that exist independently of the decision; do not create sections solely to hold alternatives. To incorporate a user-added option into a revision, keep its id and words as an ordinary lf-option. A multiple-choice Ask still needs the user's Done even when chosen is authored. Use settled to collapse a retired decision while preserving its options and anchors.
lf-options.x-example:
Where should run status appear?

Both choices preserve the existing run detail.

effort: lowrisk: medrecommended Status on the run list One join; failures are visible without a click. effort: nonerisk: low Leave the list alone No work; failures stay one click away.

lf-option.description: One alternative in a decision, shown as a compact label or a card with supporting evidence.
lf-option.x-instructions: Lead a card with a `<strong>` title and a sentence naming its consequence. Where alternatives differ in arrangement, structure, or mechanism, draw each with an svg.drawing thumbnail in the same frame, alike except where they differ. Use matching comparison chips when facts help; add paragraphs or a fact rail when the face alone cannot support the choice. A bare label suits an alternative needing no further case. Direct text uses inline Markdown; use HTML children for block content. A for target must remain useful independently of the decision and does not supply the option's words. chosen records the user's pick; a recommended chip is advice. Rewriting a picked option needs restated; read $restated for when to rewrite instead of correcting beside the Ask.

lf-chip.description: A short comparison label above an option or variant title, optionally colored by the author’s judgment.
lf-chip.x-instructions: Put the same comparison chips in the same order before each sibling's `<strong>` title. Name the facts the alternatives differ on rather than applying a fixed facet vocabulary. A final recommended chip can mark your preference; give the reason in prose, and keep it distinct from chosen. Use a dl.facts rail for a comparison needing longer explanations. Apply tone only when its judgment helps: a repeated color on every chip distinguishes nothing.

lf-milestones.description: A schedule of planned stages with status markers.
lf-milestones.x-example: Survey the sites Map sun and squirrel routes. Build the feeders Two classic, two heated. Install and watch

lf-milestone.description: One scheduled milestone with a status and optional time label.
lf-milestone.x-instructions: Lead with a `<strong>` title and follow with prose. Use when for the schedule label.

lf-chronology.description: A chronology of observed facts and interventions, such as an incident timeline.
lf-chronology.x-instructions: Write entries in the intended reading order, oldest or newest first, and bound the chronology at the end containing its newest entry.
lf-chronology.x-example: Feeder camera offline Battery alert from the north feeder. Battery swapped Camera back Feed resumed.

lf-chronology-entry.description: One observed event in a chronology, with a time label and kind.
lf-chronology-entry.x-instructions: Lead with a `<strong>` title and follow with prose. Use at for the time label.

lf-compare.description: Labeled variants presented for comparison without asking the user to choose.
lf-compare.x-instructions: Use a dl.facts rail after each variant's label when aligned comparison facts are useful. Block content in a variant stacks the group into rows; terse variants can sit side by side.
lf-compare.x-example: Cedar Weathers silver; no sealant. Pine Cheaper; seal it yearly.

lf-variant.description: One labeled variant in a comparison, with prose or widgets as its evidence.
lf-variant.x-instructions: Lead with a `<strong>` label, then place its evidence and explanation inside the variant.

lf-metric.description: A headline number with a label, optional change, and a judgment of whether that change is good.
lf-metric.x-instructions: Write the label as element text and the headline number in value. Give delta its sign. Set direction only when you can say whether an increase or decrease is good; otherwise the delta remains neutral. Place metric tiles in a layout-tiles block.
lf-metric.x-example: daily visits refills species seen

lf-tree.description: A file tree rendered from indented text, with optional change counts.
lf-tree.x-instructions: Write one node per line inside the pre, indent children deeper, mark directories with a trailing /, and add trailing +N/-N tokens for change badges. HTML-escape & before < and >.
lf-tree.x-example:
feeders/
  mount.py  +2 -2
  schedule.py  +1
  sites/
    north.toml

lf-code.description: A source-code excerpt with syntax coloring, highlighted lines, and line-anchored remarks.
lf-code.x-instructions: Write the exact code inside pre at column 0, HTML-escaping & before < and >. Set language for source code and omit it for plain transcripts or command output. For excerpts, set lines to the ascending source ranges quoted, such as 1505-1507,1520-1527; hi and lf-note at then use those source numbers. A note addressed to an omitted line captions the elided row.
lf-code.x-example:
def bracket(temp):
    if temp < 0:
        return "steel"
    return "cedar"
Freezing is the only threshold that matters.

lf-note.description: A prose remark anchored to a line or omitted range of its lf-code parent.
lf-note.x-instructions: Set at to the line number as the parent numbers it: 1-based by default, or the source number declared in lines.

lf-chart.description: An Observable Plot chart authored with Plot’s API and sized to its place in the page.
lf-chart.x-instructions: Write a JavaScript expression for Plot.plot's options inside pre, HTML-escaping & before < and >; give the options object rather than calling Plot.plot. Plot and width are the only names in scope, and data stays inline. Use ISO date strings on an explicitly typed time scale; use utc for days and months, and include a timezone on moments, such as 2026-06-01T14:00Z. Supply ariaLabel describing the chart for users who cannot see it. Leave width and height out of the options: use width to adapt ticks, and data-height on the element for a nondefault height. Where page check --render reports overlapping labels, reduce category ticks, choose them by width, or reserve more margin for the axis label. Use var(--series-N) for constant or categorical colors; continuous color scales need a Plot scheme because CSS variables cannot be interpolated. Name the chart in the surrounding heading or prose rather than Plot's title.
lf-chart.x-example:
{
  ariaLabel: "Hours to first review by week: backend fell from 31 to 12, frontend from 18 to 11",
  x: {type: "utc", ticks: "monday", label: null},
  y: {grid: true, label: "hours to first review"},
  color: {legend: true, range: ["var(--series-1)", "var(--series-2)"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.lineY(
      [
        {week: "2026-05-04", team: "backend", hours: 31},
        {week: "2026-05-11", team: "backend", hours: 26},
        {week: "2026-05-18", team: "backend", hours: 12},
        {week: "2026-05-04", team: "frontend", hours: 18},
        {week: "2026-05-11", team: "frontend", hours: 21},
        {week: "2026-05-18", team: "frontend", hours: 11},
      ],
      {x: "week", y: "hours", stroke: "team", marker: true},
    ),
  ],
}

lf-shot.description: A before-and-after screenshot comparison with an operable divider and optional change outlines.
lf-shot.x-instructions: Use served image paths printed by leaf page media for before and after, and describe the pair in alt. Read authoring-evidence.md, Source files and media, for captures and when to use outlines. Write explanations in surrounding prose rather than element content. When a decision turns on the change, put the pair inside the proposing option.
lf-shot.x-example:
The option cards

The chips now sit above the title, so a scanning eye reads cost before prose.

lf-board.description: A kanban board whose cards the user can move between columns and reorder.
lf-board.x-instructions: When revising, keep each moved card in the column the user chose unless the revision explicitly retracts that decision with restated on the card. Read authoring-revisions.md, Honor user state. A rewrite that invalidates a move restates the card, not the board.
lf-board.x-example: Heated perch Wire the south feeder. Squirrel baffle Camera mount

lf-column.description: One named board column, including empty columns the user can move a card into.
lf-column.x-instructions: Write a label that names the column on its own. Use tone when landing here carries a status judgment, such as blocked, needing review, or done; otherwise leave it neutral.

lf-card.description: One board card whose identity and comments survive user moves.
lf-card.x-instructions: Lead with a `<strong>` title and follow with prose. Keep its id stable across moves. Rewriting a card the user moved needs restated; read $restated.

lf-tabs.description: Several views of one artifact, as page navigation, a local tabbed section, or a side-list queue.
lf-tabs.x-instructions: Place the first set directly in main for page navigation; other placements make a framed local tabbed section. Put the shared title and lede before page tabs and the primary current view first. Each lf-tab is a self-contained view, while history, Threads, Asks, versions, and sign-off belong to the whole page. Retire obsolete views once current work no longer depends on them, preserving needed context and passages anchoring open threads or standing decisions in details within the relevant tab. Use list="side" for a queue beside its selected item; it remains framed and its list does not stick.
lf-tabs.x-example:
Wire the first site this week.

Keep the original outcome and constraints in reach.

lf-tab.description: One labeled view in a tab set, optionally summarized in a side-list queue.
lf-tab.x-instructions: Use summary for the few words a side-list queue needs for scanning, such as severity, age, or suggested outcome. Keep ids distinct across tabs: they share the page's one id space.

lf-draft.description: A block of text the user owns and can rewrite in place, with recorded revision history.
lf-draft.x-instructions: Write the draft text verbatim inside pre, HTML-escaping & before < and > and preserving newlines. Use a suggestion for an agent-proposed change to existing prose. A draft asks for an edit when needed is present; otherwise it is an optional editing surface. Use lf-ask when that request needs its own heading and supporting evidence, or page sign-off to approve the whole page. Preserve the user’s edits on revision. To replace an edited passage deliberately, write the new text and mark the draft restated; read $restated.
lf-draft.x-example: Adds --dry-run to every mutating command.

lf-sample.description: A quotation of page content, either static or an operable child Leaf page.
lf-sample.x-instructions: For a live child page, put its main content in one direct template[data-sample] with a stable id. Use window for a whole Leaf window including its chrome. Keep invented content visibly fictional. Read page-authoring.md, Live samples, for child-page interaction, reset, and isolation.
lf-sample.x-example: effort: lowPaper maps Nothing to charge. effort: medDedicated GPS Offline maps, week-long battery. My take: this is the better field tool.

lf-pane.description: A reading region with an optional header and footer, independently scrollable inside a full-height workspace.
lf-pane.x-instructions: For independent scrolling, place the pane as a full-height workspace’s body or a direct cell; elsewhere the page scrolls. Wrap multiple body blocks in one div or section. Use label to name the region accessibly and its header for the visible heading. Put action widgets in the direct footer when they should remain reachable as the body scrolls.
lf-pane.x-example: Read the selected record.
